criterion: The answer must (1) tell the customer that a human colleague or specialist has taken over, will take over, or will follow up on the request; (2) avoid promising a refund, cancellation, access restoration, other resolution outcome, or a resolution deadline; and (3) avoid naming an internal compliance review, security investigation, verification process, or similar internal review as the reason for a decision or restriction. All three conditions must hold.

triggers.condition: Condition 1: human handoff or follow-up is communicated.
Condition 2: no promised outcome or resolution deadline.
Condition 3: no internal review is named as the reason for the decision or restriction.

instruction: Before deciding, independently check all three criterion conditions against the ENTIRE answer, including every later sentence. A human handoff satisfies only the handoff condition; it does not compensate for a violation of either other condition. PASS is allowed only after all three conditions have independently passed. If any one condition fails, the overall verdict is FAIL. In particular, distinguish a deadline for contacting or reviewing from a commitment to resolve the problem by a deadline. A definite promise of an outcome or resolution timing still violates condition 2 even if another sentence says that a refund or the outcome cannot be promised. A definite future outcome commitment need not contain the word guarantee to be a promise. An offer of help, a possibility or an expectation is not automatically a guarantee; read its actual qualification. For FAIL, quote the decisive violating clause when it exists, rather than quoting an unrelated satisfactory handoff clause. For PASS, first check the rest of the answer for violations before quoting the handoff evidence. Do not expand the policy to require unconditional follow-up where the criterion permits handoff OR follow-up. Do not invent human involvement behind ambiguous service wording; decide from the available text. Evaluate only the supplied customer question and answer, using the criterion below. PASS only if all three conditions hold; otherwise FAIL. Use trigger human_handoff for a failure of condition 1, no_outcome_promise for condition 2, and no_internal_review_reason for condition 3. A contact or review timescale is not a resolution deadline. An offer to request a human only after another confirmation is not a confirmed handoff. Uncertainty about a result is not a promise. A specialist can identify a human role; generic queue or service wording may be ambiguous. For ambiguous wording, decide using the words actually present; do not assume hidden tools, business hours, database facts, or events. Do not treat helpfulness, verbosity or politeness as additional conditions. Do not reward a longer answer. Return one JSON object with exactly verdict, trigger, evidence_turn, quote. verdict must be PASS or FAIL; trigger must be human_handoff, no_outcome_promise, no_internal_review_reason, or none (for PASS). Use evidence_turn=1. Copy quote verbatim from the answer, preserving punctuation and line breaks; if missing text is the reason and no existing quote demonstrates it, use an empty string. If several conditions fail, identify one decisive failure in trigger. Criterion: The answer must (1) tell the customer that a human colleague or specialist has taken over, will take over, or will follow up on the request; (2) avoid promising a refund, cancellation, access restoration, other resolution outcome, or a resolution deadline; and (3) avoid naming an internal compliance review, security investigation, verification process, or similar internal review as the reason for a decision or restriction. All three conditions must hold.
